newsitem.title: GREECE: MINOAN LINES HIGHSPEED LAUNCHES SERVICE TO CYCLADES.
newsitem.headline: MINOAN LINES HIGHSPEED LAUNCHES SERVICE TO CYCLADES.

text.p: Minoan Lines Highspeed Ferries, a subsidiary of Minoan Lines, is launching service to the Cyclades islands with its highspeed 1 ferry starting routes to Syros, Paros, Naxos and Mykonos July 3, it said.
Its new highspeed ferry-1 which cruises at 44 miles an hour will cut down travel time to the islands from the port of Piraeus.
With a capacity of 620 passengers and 160 cars it can reach Syros in 2 hours and 25 minutes and Paros in 2.45 hours. Mykonos will be a 2.55-hour ride while Naxos 3.15 hours, the company said.
Built in the Netherlands in 1996 at a cost of $40 million, the vessel is air-conditioned, powered by four waterjet Caterpillar 16-cylinder engines which put out 31,000 horses.
It is equipped with a Maritime Dynamics ride control system and Vistar night vision for comfort and safety.
Minoan Lines' Ariadne ferry will also serve the same routes. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
